newsitem.title: LATVIA: Norway backs EU talks with Balts as a bloc.
newsitem.headline: Norway backs EU talks with Balts as a bloc.

text.p: Norwegian Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal said on Monday the European Union (EU) should start membership talks with all three Baltic states at the same time, rejecting a German suggestion that Estonia may be ready first.
The Baltic states quit what was then the Soviet Union in 1991 and all three have set their sights on EU and NATO membership as they seek to reintegrate with the West.
Some analysts and politicians have said Estonia, the smallest Baltic state but seen by many as the most economically advanced, may be ready for EU entry before Latvia and Lithuania.
But Godal reiterated that Scandinavia was not distinguishing between the three nations of around eight million people.
"Norway and its Nordic EU neighbours support simultaneous membership talks with the Baltic states," Godal told a news conference during a visit to Latvia.
"Efforts on the European continent to see Lithuania as closer to central and eastern Europe and Estonia being almost a part of Finland...are rubbish," Godal added.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said last week that Estonia may qualify for the EU ahead of Latvia and Lithuania and asked rhetorically whether a special case could be made for it.
"A regional approach (towards the Baltic states) has a very strong position, not only in the Nordic countries," Godal added.
Western diplomats say the Balts are unlikely to enter NATO in a first round and may have a better chance of early EU entry.
Latvian Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs said that the differences between the Baltic states were not big and were less than between some EU member states.
